answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token for a fixed period before it may post jobs or claim rewards. The protocol caps influence by locked stake, not account count, and slashes stake when an identity is proven to double-claim. Splitting funds across a spiral of accounts does not multiply voting weight; it ties up more capital and exposes more deposits to loss. Even a zephyr of new identities must pay the same real cost, whether operating in a tundra or a city.
